title: They take this from Samuel Rutherford: God's will is determined from eternity toward every being, so conditionals are true by his will
source_text: XXXIV. Porro hanc suam doctrinam fatentur illi se sumpsisse a Samuele Retorforti Scoto, ex quo, ut certissimum fundamentum, ibidem supponunt: Quod voluntas Dei ad nulla entia, vel quae actu sunt, vel quae sunt in potentia, seu aliquando actuanda, seu in actum nunquam deducenda, sit indeterminata, dubia, aut suspensa, seu habens in se potentialitatem, suspensionem & privationem actus secundi, qualis reperitur in voluntate creata, sed quod sit per eminentiam sui actus, respectu omnis entis ab aeterno determinata. Unde colligunt, Deum necessario velle, vel non velle omnes concatenationes & connexiones entium possibiles, adeoque in omnibus propositionibus conditionatis de futuro contingenti, verum esse ex definita & certa Dei voluntate, quod si talis vel talis conditio poneretur, sequeretur hoc & non aliud.
pass_a_gloss: XXXIV. Further they confess that they have taken this their doctrine from Samuel Rutherford the Scot, from whom, as a most certain foundation, they suppose in the same place: That the will of God toward no beings, either those which are in act, or which are in potency, whether to be at some time actuated, or never to be brought into act, is indeterminate, doubtful, or suspended, or having in itself potentiality, suspension and privation of second act, such as is found in a created will, but that it is by the eminence of its act, in respect of every being determined from eternity. Whence they gather, that God necessarily wills, or does not will all the possible concatenations and connections of beings, and so in all conditional propositions concerning a future contingent, it is true from the definite and certain will of God, that if such or such a condition were posited, this and not another would follow.
pass_b_english: They admit that they took this doctrine from the Scot Samuel Rutherford, and in the same place they lay down, as a most certain foundation drawn from him, the following. God's will is not undetermined, doubtful or suspended toward any being, whether actual or potential, and whether it is to be actualized at some time or never brought into act.
Nor does his will contain potentiality, suspension and the lack of a second act, as a created will does. By the eminence of its act it is determined from eternity with respect to every being.

From this they infer that God necessarily wills or does not will every possible sequence and connection of beings. So in every conditional proposition about a contingent future, it is true by God's definite and certain will that if this or that condition were in place, this and nothing else would follow.

lemmas.gloss: by the eminence of its act

choices.why: God's decree; 'decree' is kept throughout, with 'decreed' for decrevit.
